body:
# 🔍 Description
 
Increase timeout threshold for PrepareSSHKeys job

# 🤔 Rationale

The pipeline run failed because the PrepareSSHKeys job timed out after publishing its artifact. Even if the job was rerun, it would fail since an artifact with the same name already exists. This happened because the CodeQL Initialize OneBranch task took longer than usual, as it sometimes does when building the CodeQL database. This means that a new pipeline run is needed, increasing the timeout threshold should avoid most of these cases.

Note: The artifact is consumed by another job, therefore it needs a consistent name so the job attempt can't be added to the artifact name. It could be argued that to cover this type of issues we could always consume the artifact with the job attempt 1 (as that one works and the issue was just a timeout), but that seems like a more convoluted solution to this issue.

author: okolawole-ebsco
body:
## Purpose

This PR adds comprehensive transitive dependency analysis for npm/Node.js projects and enhances security through containerized execution. Previously, the tool only analyzed direct dependencies from `package.json`, missing potentially hundreds of transitive dependencies that could introduce license compliance issues.

**Key problems solved:**
- Incomplete dependency analysis - transitive dependencies were not evaluated
- Security risk - executing build commands on untrusted repositories without isolation
- npm-specific licensing complexity - SPDX expressions and dual-licensing not properly handled
- Inconsistent license issue classification - all issues treated as failures instead of appropriate severity levels

## Approach

### 1. Transitive Dependency Analysis for npm

Implemented full transitive dependency extraction using `license-checker-rseidelsohn`:

- **Primary method**: `yarn install` + `license-checker-rseidelsohn` for complete dependency tree with license information
- **Graceful fallback**: Parse `package.json` directly if license-checker fails (with prominent warnings about incomplete analysis)
- **SPDX license parsing**: Properly split and normalize SPDX expressions like `"MIT OR Apache-2.0"` into separate licenses
- **FOLIO registry support**: Auto-configures `.npmrc` for `@folio` scoped packages while respecting existing configurations
- **Security measures**: `--ignore-scripts` flag prevents execution of install hooks, timeouts enforce resource limits

### 2. Enhanced License Compliance Evaluation

Introduced structured issue classification with `LicenseIssueType` enum:

- **Category X violations** (GPL, etc.) → automatic `FAIL` status
- **Unknown licenses** → `MANUAL` review required
- **Undocumented Category B** (LGPL, MPL, EPL, CDDL) → `MANUAL` review required
- **No license information** → `MANUAL` review required
- **Parser errors** → Validation that parsers correctly split dual-licenses

This enables programmatic decision-making and clearer reporting to module maintainers.

### 3. Security-Focused Devcontainer

Created comprehensive devcontainer for isolated execution:

- **Container isolation**: Malicious build files cannot access host system
- **Complete toolchain**: Node.js 20, Java 21, Maven 3.9.9, Gradle 8.12
- **Developer experience**: zsh, git-delta, fzf, VS Code extensions pre-configured
- **Volume caching**: Maven repository, yarn cache, bash history persisted
- **Non-root user**: Runs as `node` user for additional security

### 4. Code Quality Improvements

- **Comprehensive test coverage**: 376 lines of tests for npm parser covering edge cases, fallback scenarios, and error conditions
- **Enhanced error handling**: Stack traces in error details, graceful degradation, structured error types
- **Parser contract validation**: Detects when parsers fail to split dual-licenses (validates separators, parentheses, SPDX `WITH` keyword)
- **Improved Maven timeout**: Increased from 60s to 120s for large projects
- **Better fallback warnings**: Prominent alerts when analysis is incomplete

### 5. Documentation Updates

- **Security warnings**: Clear disclosure of code execution risks
- **Usage instructions**: Devcontainer setup, GitHub Actions workflow, CLI usage
- **README enhancements**: Added note about transitive dependency analysis

This PR queries every node after storing a new message in the message canister in `assert_subnet_is_healthy`. This ensures that every node is up-to-date and has the latest message when returning.
Otherwise, this is a source of flakiness where after quickly [setting](https://sourcegraph.com/github.com/dfinity/ic/-/blob/rs/tests/nested/nns_recovery/common.rs?L227-234) a new message with this function, [breaking](https://sourcegraph.com/github.com/dfinity/ic/-/blob/rs/tests/nested/nns_recovery/common.rs?L283) the subnet, and [reading](https://sourcegraph.com/github.com/dfinity/ic/-/blob/rs/tests/nested/nns_recovery/common.rs?L284-290) the message again, the old message would be returned because the node that we are querying in this last read probably did not have the latest state (including the new message).

author: alanagoyal
body:
## Summary
- Expands the note saving architecture with a Pending Updates Queue, a single batched RPC, and optimistic UI throughout the app (including the sidebar).
- Adds immediate save triggers on blur, unmount, and beforeunload, plus a visual save status indicator.
- Removes unnecessary refetching in favor of optimistic UI and ISR revalidation.
- Introduces optimistic sidebar updates via a new SessionNotesContext API (updateNoteInContext and addNoteToContext).
- Includes mobile-note creation optimizations and a suite of new documentation and migration artifacts to support the new flow.
- Adds MOBILE_NOTE_BLANK_FIX.md to address a mobile race condition where a new note could render blank in the sidebar during rapid navigation.

## Changes

### Core
- **components/note.tsx**
  - Added pendingUpdatesRef to accumulate updates instead of replacing them.
  - Implemented performSave() to execute a single batched DB call and ISR revalidation.
  - Refactored saveNote() to queue updates and debounce with a 500ms delay.
  - Added saveImmediately() for immediate save on blur events.
  - Added unmount and beforeunload handlers to persist pending updates.
  - Introduced a local saveStatus state for UX feedback.
- **app/notes/session-notes.tsx**
  - Added updateNoteInContext(noteId, updates) to support optimistic sidebar updates.
  - Added addNoteToContext(note) to optimistically add newly created notes to the sidebar.
  - Exposes updateNoteInContext and addNoteToContext via SessionNotesContext.
- **components/note-header.tsx**
  - Display save status indicator (Saving... / Saved / Error).
  - Trigger saveImmediately() on emoji selection and title blur.
- **components/note-content.tsx**
  - Added blur handler to trigger saveImmediately().

### Backend
- **supabase/migrations/20241024_update_note_batched.sql (NEW)**
  - Adds update_note_batched(uuid_arg, session_arg, title_arg, emoji_arg, content_arg)
  - NULL arguments mean “don’t update this field”; uses COALESCE in UPDATE.
  - Drops old update_note_partial if exists; grants execute permissions.

### Documentation & Architecture
- **SAVE_ARCHITECTURE_IMPROVEMENTS.md (NEW)**
  - Deep dive into the new pending-queue, batched RPC, and UX improvements.
- **SAVE_FLOW_COMPARISON.md (NEW)**
  - Visual comparison of old vs new save flow.
- **DEPLOYMENT_CHECKLIST.md (NEW)**
  - Migration steps, verification, and testing plan for deployment.
- **ARCHITECTURE.md (UPDATED)**
  - Updated data flow and bottlenecks to reflect new approach.
- **CHANGES_SUMMARY.md (NEW)**
  - High-level changelog for this set of changes.
- **QUICK_REFERENCE.md (NEW)**
  - Quick guide to the new save flow and key metrics.
- **SIDEBAR_UPDATE_FIX.md (NEW)**
  - Documenting the optimistic context update approach to keep the UI in sync without refetching.
- **MOBILE_NOTE_CREATION_FIX.md (NEW)**
  - Optimizations to ensure mobile note creation appears in the sidebar immediately.
- **MOBILE_NOTE_BLANK_FIX.md (NEW)**
  - Fixes a mobile race where a newly created note could render blank in the sidebar during fast navigation.

## How it Works (Technical)
- Debounced saves now accumulate updates in pendingUpdatesRef instead of cancelling prior work.
- After 500ms of inactivity, performSave() executes with ALL accumulated updates:
  - Single batched RPC call: update_note_batched with NULL-based partial updates:
    - title_arg: value or NULL if not updated
    - emoji_arg: value or NULL if not updated
    - content_arg: value or NULL if not updated
  - ISR cache is invalidated via /notes/revalidate; no refreshSessionNotes() or router.refresh() calls are made.
- UI updates optimistically in real time; a visual save status is shown next to the note’s Private badge.
- Immediate saves are triggered on blur for title/content, emoji selection, and on unmount/beforeunload to reduce data loss risk.
- Auto-retry on error is implemented to handle transient failures.
- Sidebar now updates instantly via updateNoteInContext() and addNoteToContext() to reflect changes without DB round-trips.

### Note Creation and Sidebar Optimizations
- Mobile and desktop note creation flows now optimistically update the sidebar so new notes appear immediately (via addNoteToContext and SessionNotesContext).
- Command Menu and New Note flows were updated to pass addNoteToContext to createNote operations.

### Data Flow Summary
- Before: separate debounced RPCs with possible race conditions and full refetches.
- After: a single batched RPC handles all field updates; ISR handles cache invalidation; optimistic context updates keep the UI in sync without extra DB queries.

## Migration Plan
- Run the database migration to create update_note_batched:
  - supabase db push
  - Or apply manually via SQL: apply /supabase/migrations/20241024_update_note_batched.sql
- Verify function exists:
  - SELECT routine_name FROM information_schema.routines WHERE routine_name = 'update_note_batched';
- Test in development/staging with the scenarios described in the Testing Plan below.

## Testing Plan
Critical
- Title Save Race Condition:
  1) Create a new note
  2) Type title, then immediately switch to content within 500ms
  3) Type content and wait ~1s
  4) Refresh page and verify both title and content are saved

Additional
- Blur Save: edit title, blur the field, ensure Saving... then Saved appears
- Emoji Save: select an emoji, ensure immediate save behavior and UI feedback
- Rapid multi-field edits: title + emoji + content within a few seconds; verify all fields saved
- Save on navigation: edit then navigate away and back; verify data persisted
- Save on tab close: trigger beforeunload path and confirm prompt and data persistence
- Error handling: simulate network issues; verify “Error - Retrying...” appears and auto-retry succeeds

Performance & QA
- Confirm ~60% reduction in DB calls per save (batched RPC vs multiple RPCs + refetches)
- Verify ISR revalidation path is sufficient for public notes

## Rollout Plan
- Deploy to staging first, run all tests across multiple devices/network conditions
- Monitor for any anomalies in save flow and revert if needed
- Proceed to production once validated

## Migration & Rollback
- Migration: apply update_note_batched.sql (as described above)
- Rollback: if issues arise, drop function public.update_note_batched; revert code changes as needed

## Documentation & References
- SAVE_ARCHITECTURE_IMPROVEMENTS.md – detailed technical explanation
- SAVE_FLOW_COMPARISON.md – before/after flow diagrams
- ARCHITECTURE.md – updated with new data flow
- DEPLOYMENT_CHECKLIST.md – deployment steps and testing guide
- CHANGES_SUMMARY.md – high-level changes overview
- QUICK_REFERENCE.md – quick guide to new save flow and metrics
- SIDEBAR_UPDATE_FIX.md – optimistic context update approach documentation
- MOBILE_NOTE_CREATION_FIX.md – mobile creation optimization details
- MOBILE_NOTE_BLANK_FIX.md – mobile race fix for blank notes

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Batched update saves all changed fields in a single DB call
- [x] Pending updates do not cancel each other; race conditions prevented
- [x] Save on blur, unmount, and beforeunload functioning
- [x] Visual save status is accurate and auto-clears after a short duration
- [x] No unnecessary refetching; ISR revalidation remains the only cache invalidation
- [x] Auto-retry on error is implemented and tested
- [x] Migration can be applied in production with a clear rollback path

## Rollout Notes
- The new SIDEBAR_UPDATE_FIX.md documents the optimistic context update approach to keep the UI in sync without extra queries. This work complements the existing architecture changes and is included in the Changes and Documentation artifacts above.

## 🐞 Descripción del Problema Al generar un corte desde la app EDS, el mensaje de WhatsApp que se envía con el resumen del turno mostraba una **EDS incorrecta**, diferente a la que realmente está asociada al **islero** que realizó el corte. **Ejemplo del bug:** - En la tabla `islander`, el usuario **Apolo** tiene asociado `id_eds = 2` (EDS prueba) - Sin embargo, el mensaje de WhatsApp mostraba: ``` 📋 CORTE EDS LA LABRANZA SAS 👨‍💼 Islero: Apolo ``` Esto causaba confusión en la administración y afectaba la trazabilidad de datos financieros y operativos por estación. ## 🔍 Causa Raíz El código en `SendWhatsAppMessageCommandHandler.cs` estaba usando `court.IdEds` para obtener el nombre de la EDS mostrada en el mensaje de WhatsApp. Sin embargo, según la estructura de la base de datos, cada islero tiene su propia EDS asociada en la tabla `islander` a través de la columna `id_eds`. **Código anterior (línea 196):** ```csharp // Obtener el nombre de la EDS var edsResult = await edsGetByIdService.GetByIdAsync(court.IdEds); ``` ## ✅ Solución Implementada Modificado el código para usar el `IdEds` del islero que realizó el corte, con un fallback al `court.IdEds` para garantizar robustez en caso de que el islero no se encuentre. **Código actualizado:** ```csharp // Obtener el nombre de la EDS - usar la EDS del islero, no la del corte var edsId = islero?.IdEds ?? court.IdEds; var edsResult = await edsGetByIdService.GetByIdAsync(edsId); ``` ## 📋 Cambios Realizados - **Archivo modificado**: `Poliedro.Eds.Application/SendMessage/Commands/SendWhatsAppMessageCommandHandler.cs` - **Líneas modificadas**: 195-197 (3 líneas) - **Tipo de cambio**: Corrección de lógica de negocio ## 🎯 Impacto ### Positivo - ✅ El mensaje de WhatsApp ahora muestra la **EDS correcta** asociada al islero - ✅ Reportes de ventas y flujo de efectivo correctamente atribuidos por estación - ✅ Mejora la trazabilidad de datos financieros y operativos - ✅ Elimina confusión en la administración al recibir información precisa ### Cambios Técnicos - ✅ Cambio mínimo y quirúrgico (solo 3 líneas modificadas) - ✅ Incluye fallback defensivo para prevenir errores si el islero no existe - ✅ No afecta ninguna otra funcionalidad del sistema - ✅ Compatible con el código existente ## 🧪 Verificación - ✅ **Compilación**: Proyecto compila exitosamente sin nuevos errores ni warnings - ✅ **Code Review**: Sin problemas detectados - ✅ **Análisis de Seguridad (CodeQL)**: Sin vulnerabilidades encontradas - ✅ **Impacto**: Cambio mínimo y controlado ## 🏷️ Referencias Relacionado con: #[número del issue] Etiquetas: `bug` `backend` `whatsapp` `corte` `data-integrity` `alta-prioridad`

# Pull Request: TravelPass - Decentralized Travel Experience Platform

## 🎯 Overview

This PR introduces **TravelPass**, a comprehensive blockchain-based travel platform that revolutionizes how travelers discover destinations, share experiences, book itineraries, and connect with local guides while earning rewards for their contributions.

## 📋 Summary

TravelPass is a feature-rich smart contract built in Clarity for the Stacks blockchain. It combines destination management, experience sharing, itinerary planning, local guide marketplace, and achievement systems with a native token economy to create an engaging global travel community.

## ✨ Key Features

### 1. Global Destination Registry
- **Add Destinations**: Users can contribute travel destinations worldwide
- **Rich Metadata**: Name, country, city, category, description, and GPS coordinates
- **Categorization System**: Five predefined categories (urban, nature, beach, mountain, cultural)
- **Statistics Tracking**: Automatic tracking of visitors, ratings, and review counts
- **Verification System**: Admin verification for quality assurance
- **Average Ratings**: Dynamic calculation based on check-in ratings (1-100 scale)

### 2. Traveler Profile System
- **Five Traveler Types**: Explorer, Adventurer, Backpacker, Luxury, Business
- **Progressive Leveling**: 10-level ranking system
- **Comprehensive Statistics**:
  - Countries visited counter
  - Total reviews written
  - Total check-ins completed
  - Guide sessions conducted
  - Reputation score (starting at 100)
  - Join date and last activity timestamps
- **Customizable**: Update username and traveler type
- **Auto-Initialization**: Profiles created automatically on first interaction

### 3. Check-in System
- **Destination Verification**: Must check in before sharing experiences
- **Detailed Logging**: Stay duration, travel companions, experience rating, personal notes
- **One-Time Restriction**: Prevents duplicate check-ins per destination
- **Automatic Updates**:
  - Increments destination visitor count
  - Updates destination average rating
  - Increases traveler check-in count
  - Advances traveler level based on difficulty
  - Boosts reputation score (+5 points)
- **Token Rewards**: 1.5 TPJ per check-in
- **Rating Scale**: 1-100 for nuanced feedback

### 4. Experience Sharing System
- **Multiple Content Types**: Reviews, guides, tips, stories
- **Rich Content**: Up to 512 characters for detailed storytelling
- **Photo Integration**: Track photo count with bonus rewards
- **Rating System**: 1-100 scale matching check-in ratings
- **Community Engagement**: Helpful votes from other travelers
- **Verification Flag**: Admin can verify high-quality content
- **Access Control**: Must check in at destination before sharing
- **Photo Bonus**: Extra 1 TPJ for experiences with 3+ photos
- **Token Rewards**: 3 TPJ per experience shared
- **Statistics**: Updates destination review count and traveler profile

### 5. Travel Itinerary Marketplace
- **Comprehensive Planning**: Title, description, duration, budget range, trip type
- **Budget Categories**: Budget, mid-range, luxury
- **Trip Types**: Solo, couple, family, group
- **Difficulty Levels**: 1-5 scale for complexity
- **Creator Requirements**: Must be traveler level 3+
- **Booking System**:
  - Other travelers can book published itineraries
  - Prevents self-booking
  - Tracks booking date, travel date, group size
  - Status management (booked, completed, cancelled)
  - Feedback tracking system
  - Prevents duplicate bookings
- **Popularity Tracking**: Automatic booking counter
- **Active/Inactive Toggle**: Creators can manage availability

### 6. Local Guide Marketplace
- **Service Registration**: Guides offer expertise at specific destinations
- **Detailed Profiles**:
  - Service title and description (up to 200 chars)
  - Specialties listing (up to 128 chars)
  - Hourly rate setting (flexible pricing)
  - Languages spoken (up to 64 chars)
  - Total bookings counter
  - Average rating from clients
- **Strict Requirements**:
  - Minimum 150 reputation score
  - Minimum 10 check-ins at destinations
  - Prevents duplicate service offerings per destination
- **Booking Management**:
  - Prevents self-booking
  - Future date validation
  - Automatic cost calculation (hourly rate × duration)
  - Status tracking (booked, completed, cancelled)
  - Client rating system (1-100)
- **Session Completion**:
  - Guide completes session and provides client rating
  - Updates guide statistics
  - Boosts reputation (+rating/10 points)

body:
## Problem

The controller_manager was unable to receive the `robot_description` topic from `robot_state_publisher`, preventing the entire ros2_control stack from initializing. This critical issue blocked all robot functionality including:

- ❌ Motor control (VESC hardware interface failed to load)
- ❌ TF tree publication (base_link, odom, wheel frames)
- ❌ RTAB-Map SLAM ("base_link does not exist", "TF of received laser scan topic is not set")
- ❌ Voice command execution (commands couldn't reach motors)
- ❌ diff_drive_controller activation
- ❌ Odometry publication
- ❌ Nav2 navigation

**Root Cause:** After Zenoh namespace integration, the remapping syntax in `start_ros2_control.sh` was incorrect. The `robot_state_publisher` publishes to `/robot_description`, but `controller_manager` subscribes to `~/robot_description` which resolves to `/controller_manager/robot_description`, creating a namespace mismatch.

## Solution

### 1. Fixed remapping syntax in `start_ros2_control.sh`

**Before:**
```bash
exec ros2 run controller_manager ros2_control_node \
    --ros-args \
    --params-file ${CONTROLLER_CONFIG} \
    -r /controller_manager/robot_description:=/robot_description
```

**After:**
```bash
exec ros2 run controller_manager ros2_control_node \
    --ros-args \
    --params-file ${CONTROLLER_CONFIG} \
    --remap ~/robot_description:=/robot_description
```

The `~/` prefix properly resolves to the node's namespace (`/controller_manager/robot_description`), and `--remap` correctly maps it to the global `/robot_description` topic published by `robot_state_publisher`.

### 2. Added explicit topic parameter in `controller_manager.yaml`

```yaml
controller_manager:
  ros__parameters:
    update_rate: 50
    # FIX: Явно указываем топик robot_description
    robot_description_topic: /robot_description
    controller_names:
      - joint_state_broadcaster
      - diff_drive_controller
```

This provides redundancy and follows ros2_control best practices by explicitly specifying the topic.

## Impact

After this fix, the complete control pipeline will work:

✅ `controller_manager` receives `robot_description` from `robot_state_publisher`  
✅ `VescSystemHardwareInterface` loads successfully  
✅ TF tree is published (base_link, odom, wheel frames)  
✅ RTAB-Map processes laser scans correctly  
✅ Voice commands reach motors via `diff_drive_controller`  
✅ `diff_drive_controller` activates and accepts `/cmd_vel` commands  
✅ Odometry is published to `/odom`  
✅ Nav2 navigation stack operates properly  

## Testing

To verify the fix:
```bash
# Restart ros2-control container
docker-compose restart ros2-control

# Check logs for successful subscription
docker logs ros2-control | grep "robot_description"

# Verify controller status
docker exec ros2-control ros2 control list_controllers

# Check TF tree
docker exec ros2-control ros2 run tf2_tools view_frames
```

## Files Changed

- `docker/main/scripts/ros2_control/start_ros2_control.sh` (1 line)
- `docker/main/config/controllers/controller_manager.yaml` (3 lines)

Running `npx @elevenlabs/cli@latest components add orb` errored:

> ~/code/cli pennyroyalte…cn-repo-pull ❯ npx @elevenlabs/cli@latest components add orb
> Launching shadcn/ui CLI...
> Source: https://ui.elevenlabs.io
> 
> 
> 
> Something went wrong. Please check the error below for more details.
> If the problem persists, please open an issue on GitHub.
> 
> Message:
> The item at https://ui.shadcn.com/r/styles/new-york-v4/orb.json was not found. It may not exist at the registry.
> 
> Suggestion:
> Check if the item name is correct and the registry URL is accessible.

this was because default shadcn registry was used instead of custom one. This PR fixes it.
